# DateTimeSetTimeUsage

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" /> <Badge type="info" text="PHP ≤ 7.0" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs) · PhpStorm name: `DateTimeSetTimeUsageInspection`

The microseconds argument of `DateTime::setTime()` / `date_time_set()` only
exists since PHP 7.1. On older versions passing it makes the call fail and
return `false`, so the extra argument is a bug when targeting PHP < 7.1.

## Example

Target PHP 7.0:

```php{6,7,10,11}
<?php
class Clock extends DateTime {}

function rewind_clock(DateTime $d, Clock $c, DateTimeImmutable $i, $usec)
{
    $d->setTime(8, 30, 0, $usec);
    $c->setTime(8, 30, 0, 250);
    $d->setTime(8, 30, 0);
    $i->setTime(8, 30, 0, 250);
    date_time_set($d, 8, 30, 0, 0);
    \date_time_set($d, 8, 30, 0, null);
    date_time_set($d, 8, 30, 0);
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 6: Microseconds argument requires PHP 7.1+; on this version the call returns false.</li>
<li>line 7: Microseconds argument requires PHP 7.1+; on this version the call returns false.</li>
<li>line 10: Microseconds argument requires PHP 7.1+; on this version the call returns false.</li>
<li>line 11: Microseconds argument requires PHP 7.1+; on this version the call returns false.</li>
</ul>

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "DateTimeSetTimeUsage": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file), either of:

```php
// @custos-ignore DateTimeSetTimeUsage

/**
 * @noinspection DateTimeSetTimeUsageInspection
 */
```
